key_insight: PRISM automates multi-phase CT subtraction for RCC by combining registration, segmentation, and color-coded enhancement mapping into a reproducible DSA-style workflow.
clinical_relevance: It could reduce subjective phase-by-phase interpretation and speed up renal tumor characterization, while preserving high-resolution visualization for review.
method: Automated DICOM phase classification, then deep-learning isotropic upsampling with RIFE.
Kidney segmentation with TotalSegmentator v2 followed by enhancement-based tissue detection.
Three-stage registration (rigid, affine, B-spline) in SimpleITK and dual-channel subtraction display.
evidence_signal: The authors ran 200 registrations across five patients and five experiments, showing a 40 mm B-spline grid, 5% sampling, and a single-level pyramid achieved near-optimal quality with lower compute cost.
watch_item: Results come from a small, retrospective optimization study, so performance and robustness in broader patient populations and varied scanners still need validation.
paper_title: PRISM: Phase-Resolved Isotropic Subtraction Mapping for Automated Multi-Phase CT Digital Subtraction Angiography
